verses.53:1: Lord, who believed our message? And to whom was the arm of the Lord revealed?
verses.53:2: We announced before Him as a child, as a root in thirsty ground; He has no form or glory. And we saw Him, and He had no form or beauty;
verses.53:3: but His form was without honor and failing beyond the sons of men; He was a man in plague and knowing how to bear sickness, because His face has been turned away; He was dishonored and not reckoned.
verses.53:4: This One bears our sins and suffers anguish for us, and we reckoned Him to be in pain and in plague and in affliction.
verses.53:5: But He was wounded because of our sins, and He has been made sick because of our lawless deeds; the discipline of our peace was upon Him; by His bruise we were healed.
verses.53:6: All of us went astray like sheep; each man went astray in his own way; and the Lord handed Him over to our sins.
verses.53:7: And He, because He has been afflicted, does not open His mouth; like a sheep He was led to slaughter, and like a lamb before the one shearing it is silent, so He does not open His mouth.
verses.53:8: In His humiliation His judgment was taken away; who will describe His generation? For His life is taken away from the earth; because of the lawless deeds of My people He was led to death.
verses.53:9: And I will give the wicked in exchange for His burial, and the rich in exchange for His death; because He did no lawlessness, nor was there deceit in His mouth.
verses.53:10: And the Lord desires to cleanse Him from the plague. If you give an offering for sin, our soul will see a long-lived seed.
verses.53:11: And the Lord desires to take away from the pain of His soul, to show Him light and to form Him with understanding, to justify a righteous one who serves many well; and He Himself will bear their sins.
verses.53:12: Therefore He will inherit many, and He will divide the spoils of the strong, because His soul was handed over to death, and He was reckoned among the lawless; and He Himself bore the sins of many, and because of their lawless deeds He was handed over.

notes.53:1: ἀκοή means "what is heard," that is, a report or message. The verbs are aorists. The Greek adds the address "Lord" at the start, as quoted in John 12:38 and Romans 10:16.
notes.53:2: ἀνηγγείλαμεν means "we announced"; this is the Greek's own reading and differs from the Hebrew "he grew up." Pronouns for the Servant are capitalized, following NASB-style practice for this messianic passage. "Before Him" may refer to the Lord.
notes.53:3: πληγή (a blow, stroke or plague) is rendered "plague" throughout the chapter (53:3, 4, 10), so that "cleanse Him from the plague" in 53:10 keeps the link. λογίζομαι is rendered "reckon" in 53:3, 4 and 12.
notes.53:4: The Greek reads "bears our sins," not "griefs," and its verbs are present tense, kept here.
notes.53:5: παιδεία means "discipline, correction, instruction." μώλωψ is a welt or bruise left by a blow; the singular "bruise" follows the Greek.
notes.53:8: This is the Greek form quoted in Acts 8:32–33. ἀπὸ τῶν ἀνομιῶν can mean "because of" or "from" the lawless deeds; "because of" fits the context.
notes.53:9: In the Greek the Lord speaks in the first person, "I will give the wicked in exchange for His burial." This differs from the Hebrew and is rendered as it stands.
notes.53:10: The Saints Greek Critical Text reads ἡμῶν ("our soul"); many editions read ὑμῶν ("your soul"). The rendering follows the Saints text. περὶ ἁμαρτίας is the standard Septuagint expression for a sin offering.
notes.53:11: The Greek infinitives are kept in sequence ("to take away... to show... to form... to justify"). πλάσαι τῇ συνέσει, "to form (Him) with understanding," is the Greek's own wording.
notes.53:12: ἀνθ᾽ ὧν means "in return for which," that is, "because." παραδίδωμι is rendered "hand over" in 53:6 and 53:12.
